2G is a unique sampler instrument developed by Scrap Brain Audio that draws inspiration from the nostalgic sounds and aesthetics of early-2000s mobile phones. Its core purpose is to enable musicians, sound designers, and producers to create distinctive audio samples by simply describing the sound they envision. Leveraging advanced Neural Synthesis technology, 2G generates custom sound samples that users can then edit and play using their MIDI keyboard, offering a highly creative and intuitive approach to sound design. At the heart of 2G’s capabilities is its Neural Synthesis engine, which interprets user input descriptions to produce original sounds. results.content:
## Description

2G is a compact sampler instrument from Scrap Brain Audio that turns either generated audio or your own short files into playable keyboard sounds. Its early-2000s-phone design is not just visual: the optional small-speaker mode makes a deliberately narrow, 16 kHz mono character part of the instrument.

Neural Synthesis starts from a text description, then places the resulting audio in the sampler for editing and playback. Generation credits are separate from the core sampler, so saved sounds and imported samples remain usable when no credits are available. [...] Initial Audio SourceLab 2

## Key Features

 Neural Synthesis turns a text description into audio that can be edited and played in the sampler.
 Import WAV, AIFF, FLAC, or MP3 files up to 20 MB and 10 seconds long.
 Trim samples and shape playback with attack, release, brightness, detune, noise, quality, and formant controls.
 Loop analysis compares timbre, volume, and vibrato to suggest up to three smoother sustain-loop candidates.
 Root-note analysis detects a consistent pitch, corrects fine tuning on playback, and marks unpitched material when appropriate.
 The optional small-speaker simulation models mobile-device resonances and voice-coil compression, with a bypassable 16 kHz mono mode.
 The local sampler supports unlimited personal samples independently of Neural Synthesis credits. [...] Help shape SoundShockAudio. Take a 2-minute survey
